page: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a dedicated general-purpose cloud instance operating under the QEMU hypervisor. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical AMD EPYC cores at a base clock of 2.0 GHz with two threads per core. The memory subsystem provides 16.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of roughly 3.91 GB per logical core. CPU instruction support includes AVX, AES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 extensions and hardware matrix accelerators are absent. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator, but bundles 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Performance evaluation reveals distinct single-core advantages paired with lower multi-core and memory throughput. The server records strong single-thread metrics, including 1986.0 on Geekbench single-core, 2692.67 on stress-ng single-core, and 13.84 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, parallel and data-intensive benchmarks reflect resource constraints: Geekbench multi-core registers at 4602.0, PassMark CPU at 7638.8, and software compilation via Clang reaches 5772.0. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth caps at 36.09 GB/s, while database operations, Redis SET performance (4.05 million operations per second), and medium-sized LLM prompt processing remain in lower benchmark percentiles.

The ccx23 configuration represents a cost-effective option for workloads requiring predictable CPU allocation without the noise of shared-core hosting. While limited memory bandwidth and a 4-vCPU envelope curtail extreme parallel compilation, heavy database throughput, or intensive local AI inference, its dedicated AMD EPYC cores deliver steady compute cycles. It fits general-purpose tasks such as text processing, moderate web application serving, CI/CD worker nodes, and backend processing queues where dedicated resources are necessary.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a dedicated-vCPU general-purpose virtual server hosted on QEMU. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM (a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio) and 160 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The hardware includes AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions and contains no GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, ccx23 demonstrates strong single-core performance, recording 1986.0 on Geekbench single-core and 2692.67 on stress-ng. However, aggregate multi-threaded throughput and memory-intensive operations, such as Redis SET commands and software compilation, score in lower tiers due to core count limitations and constrained memory bandwidth. Without bundled public IPv4 addresses, ccx23 delivers cost-efficient dedicated compute capacity well suited for single-threaded processing, moderate web services, lightweight background workers, and standard business applications requiring stable CPU resources.
